releases.title: Explained, shared and open to more of New Eden
changes: Every surprising number now has a "?": why a wider area or more processing can show a bit less ISK, why higher tiers often give the same plan, how your weekly time is estimated, the yield estimate and shared deposits. A plain-English glossary explains the PI words AstraCore uses.
Plan outside Delve: choose "Haul to Jita / Amarr myself" and the planner sells to visible buy orders there. The Selling question only offers the routes your drop-off can actually reach.
The Advanced planner shows changes as a preview first; your guided answers only change when you press Apply these settings.

One Community page: your reports with their status in plain words, a thank-you when you send one, an optional "Reported by" credit with the character you choose, and a "This would help me" button on roadmap directions and ideas. You get a notice when something you reported or marked goes live.
The Area page writes planet types in full and shows security as a readable range.
On iPhones the strip behind the status bar stays solid in both themes, and the browser bar follows your light or dark theme.
limitations: Your own trips to a trade hub are not priced: journey time, fuel and loss risk are yours to weigh.
Plans are still estimates; yield is estimated until your own extractors have run.
technical: Sovereignty is read from ESI's current /sovereignty/systems/ route (served only at the root, not under /latest); the ESI compatibility date is 2026-08-18.
New additive database migrations v8 (community marks, credit choices, report stages) and v9 (seen live marks). The data export includes them.
Other community tools: we talk to their authors before building what they already do (docs/third-party.md).

releases.title: Clearer, steadier and kinder to your time
changes: Home, Plan, Operate and Characters: one simple menu. Area and Settings live under Plan, also on phones, and "Report a bug" is always in the menu.

"An hour of my time is worth" now shapes the plan itself: the more your time is worth, the less hauling, travelling and factory restocking the planner asks for. The guided setup and the Advanced planner use the same setting.
The same answers always give the same plan, about five times faster, and the plan you see is exactly the plan you save, download and track on Operate.
Factories are only planned when their storage lasts a full extractor cycle, so the plan fits the login rhythm you chose.
Calmer plan results: notes are grouped into a short "Before you build" box with links straight to the answer that changes them. Feeder miners say which factory they supply instead of showing 0 ISK.

Operate opens with a Next up list of the most urgent actions and is split into Build, Upkeep, Sell and Income. It refreshes your characters by itself when the data is old, and only counts PI contracts, sales and taxes. Home shows the top three actions.

Selling advice keeps one hangar on one trade hub unless a second trip really pays, never sends high-sec stock to null-sec pickups, and treats market data that didn't load as "not checked" instead of "no buyers".

Easier first steps: the welcome page shows which characters can plan PI and what to train, explains how to add alts from another EVE account, and the landing page says up front that AstraCore is free, invite-only and read-only.
A tidier profile page, a printable plan with a build checklist, a wizard that fits a phone screen, and friendlier pages when EVE's servers don't answer.
limitations: Set and forget plans can earn less than before: they now really ask less of your time. Pick Balanced or lower the value of your time for more ISK.
Plans are still estimates: yield, prices, taxes and hauling can change. Yield is estimated until your own extractors have run.
Selling and courier options are built around Delve and VOC Hauling. Other areas work with self-hauling; more choice is planned.
technical: Solves stop on a fixed number of search steps instead of a 6-second clock, and comparison cards and the plan result share one cache.

ESI: the cache is respected on refresh (no forced re-fetches), requests carry a proper user agent and a pinned compatibility date, outages fall back to the last stored public data, and only real outages make other requests wait.

Security and privacy: cached EVE data is kept per character and deleted with it, profile merging is restricted to a profile's last character, token encryption supports key rotation, and the data export includes feedback reports.
New database migrations up to schema version 7 (additive).

releases.title: First public preview
changes: Plan Planetary Interaction across all your characters with a guided setup that compares income, your weekly time and how certain the income is, and lets you go back to any answer without losing the others.

See whether each product can really be sold where AstraCore recommends: visible buyers, recent daily trades, what a full batch fetches, estimated sell-order times and how fresh the market data is. Plans steer around markets that can't take your output.

Start a plan with a first-build checklist: a copyable Multibuy list of command centers and optional starter stock, the cheapest place to buy them including courier costs, startup costs, whether each template fits its planet, and step-by-step build instructions per character. Take it with you in the plan export or the shopping list CSV.

Operate your colonies with an upkeep schedule worked out per colony: extractor restarts, factory restocks, collections when storage fills and market shipments, with shortages, output against the plan, unrouted structures and data freshness.
Follow the roadmap, suggest ideas and report bugs from the platform, and read release notes here.
A new look across the site, with motion, a clearer menu and navigation that works with one touch on phones.
technical: AstraCore now uses 0.MINOR.PATCH versions while it's in preview. Release notes are written for minor releases; the smaller updates in between are numbered automatically (0.1.1, 0.1.2, …) and described by their commits on GitHub.
Builds before this release were numbered 1.0 to 1.2.4 during early development. Their changes are part of 0.1.0; the commit history keeps the details.
The source is available under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; third-party material retains its own terms.
limitations: PI forecasts depend on yield, market prices, taxes and hauling assumptions. Yield is an estimate until your own extractors have run.
AstraCore can't buy, sell or place market orders for you. Courier rates in the return direction are estimated from VOC's published Delve → hub rates.
Fittings, PvP and fleet preparation are community directions, not available modules or promised dates.
